summary:
I've been building Keikochō, a Japanese-learning app I use myself, and this stretch was mostly about making the practice honest rather than adding new drills. The engine grades a conversation exchange through two separate code paths depending on the mode (listen/reply vs. build/assemble), and I'd wired a new scene-context note into only one of them — nothing crashed, half the modes just quietly stayed bare. Same week I found a reply board where 43% of the "pick the right answer" options were four copies of the correct answer, because the distractor picker deduped candidates by internal ID while grading compared the displayed text. Neither bug threw an error; both just made practice easier than it looked, which is the failure mode I've learned to watch for now — I write tests that check the population a rule applies to, not just whether it currently passes.

I also shipped a page rehearsing a short bilingual speech, half English and half Japanese, and learned the hard way that a Japanese farewell needs different content from an English one, not a translation of it — a direct rendering of a self-deprecating joke reads fine in English and lands wrong in Japanese, so I wrote the two halves to say related but distinct things. The build itself broke twice on my phone before it worked: opening it as a raw HTML file skipped the viewport meta tag entirely (Safari rendered it zoomed out at desktop width), and I'd embedded all the audio as base64 in one document, which iOS Safari won't reliably play. Serving it properly, with real audio files instead of embedded data, fixed both.

On the automation side, I run a personal home-agent (Hermes) on a small home server, and swapped its local model for a differently-tuned variant this week. The new model quietly stopped calling tools at all — it would type out something that looked like a tool call as plain text instead of actually invoking it. Took a while to trace because nothing errored; the fix turned out to be a single generation parameter the new model needed set differently than the old one assumed.

highlights.oneLiner: Swapped local brain model; fixed a reasoning-budget param that silently killed tool calls
